question: What will happen if the new oil filter is not soaked in oil before installing it when changing the engine oil?
solution:
The correct answer is __Oil level drops**(Option 3)**.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• If a new oil filter is not soaked in oil before installation, it can lead to a delay in proper oil circulation in the engine.
 
• This delay can cause a temporary drop in oil level as the filter absorbs oil to fill its capacity.
 
• It may also cause engine wear during the initial startup due to lack of proper lubrication.
 
• Soaking the oil filter ensures immediate oil flow to critical engine components.
 
• Proper pre-soaking reduces the risk of engine damage caused by oil starvation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Engine Noise:**
 
 
• Increased engine noise may occur temporarily if the oil filter is not primed, but it is not a direct consequence of skipping the oil soak.
 
 
 
• **Engine Overheating:**
 
 
• Skipping the oil soak is unlikely to directly cause engine overheating; overheating is more commonly linked to issues with the cooling system.
 
 
 
• **Filter Clogging:**
 
 
• A new filter is unlikely to clog immediately even if it is not soaked, as clogging is typically caused by extended use or contaminants in the oil.
